System Architecture · Overview

Audio Studio System Overview & ADRs

A self-contained platform for evaluating, scoring, and comparing speech synthesis (TTS) and speech recognition (ASR) machine learning models for the Khmer language.

1. What Audio Studio Does

Audio Studio solves a specific problem in speech machine learning research: evaluating how well speech models pronounce words and recognize natural human speech. Automated metrics (such as Word Error Rate or acoustic loss numbers) do not accurately reflect whether a computer-generated voice sounds natural or mispronounces tone and syllables in Khmer.

The platform provides two primary interfaces that communicate with a single Python standard library backend and a local SQLite database:

Admin & Researcher Portal

Path: public/admin.html

  • Study Creator: A 4-step wizard to upload WAV audio files, match transcripts via CSV, assemble modular test components on an interactive canvas, and launch evaluation campaigns.
  • Active Studies: Manage live evaluation studies, inspect evaluator completion rates, toggle study status, or delete campaigns.
  • Results & Analytics: Compute Mean Opinion Scores (MOS) with 95% confidence intervals, rater consensus agreements, and export full CSV audit ledgers.

Rater & Evaluator Portal

Path: public/eval.html

  • Frictionless Registration: Evaluators enter their name or pseudonym; no account or password creation required.
  • Audio Waveform Deck: Interactive 76px waveform canvas with playback scrubbing, speed controls (0.8x, 1.0x, 1.2x), and telephone call audio simulation (8 kHz bandpass filter).
  • Hold-and-Drag Defect Tagging: Listeners drag across the waveform or click Khmer word pills to flag mispronunciations, awkward pauses, and robotic buzzes.
  • Listening Verification: Evaluators type what they actually heard to generate real-time visual text diffs against expected transcripts.

3. Architectural Decision Records (ADRs)

ADR-01 Zero Third-Party Python Dependencies Accepted Invariant

Decision: The backend must run completely on Python's built-in standard library without installing packages via pip.

Rationale: Audio Studio is an academic thesis and research platform. Avoiding third-party dependencies eliminates dependency drift, broken virtual environments, C-extension build failures, and security vulnerabilities. Any computer with Python 3.8+ can clone the repository and run python3 run_server.py in under two seconds.

ADR-02 Single-File Local SQLite Persistence with Enforced Foreign Keys Accepted Invariant

Decision: Use a local SQLite file (workbench.db) with PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON; and parameterized SQL queries.

Rationale: Academic evaluations require absolute data durability without managing separate database servers (PostgreSQL or MySQL). SQLite commits transactions directly to the local solid-state drive with full ACID reliability. Deleting a test campaign automatically cascades to remove related evaluations and defect tags cleanly.

ADR-03 Cloudflare Tunnel Outbound Host Ingress for $0 Zero-Risk Public Hosting Accepted Invariant

Decision: Expose the local server to public evaluators using Cloudflare Tunnel (via run_server.py --share) rather than deploying to free cloud containers (such as Render or Koyeb).

Rationale: Free cloud container tiers use ephemeral filesystems that erase all local file changes when an idle instance sleeps. Hosting on a local machine via Cloudflare Tunnel guarantees that the SQLite database and physical WAV audio files are never wiped, requires no credit card, and eliminates 50-second cold-start connection timeouts.

ADR-04 HTTP 206 Partial Content Range Streaming for Audio Assets Accepted Invariant

Decision: Implement native byte-range parsing in run_server.py to support HTTP Range: bytes=start-end headers.

Rationale: Modern desktop and mobile browsers require HTTP 206 Partial Content responses to scrub through audio timelines and calculate duration metadata before the entire file finishes downloading. Without range request support, mobile browsers stall when loading uncompressed WAV audio.

4. Repository Invariants Checklist

Invariant Verification Gate Enforcement Mechanism
Zero Pip Packages Enforced scripts/validate_package.py verifies zero third-party packages are imported.
Automated Test Suite Enforced 24 automated tests run in under 2 seconds via python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v.
Admin PIN Boundaries Enforced All administrative API routes (/api/admin/*) require X-Admin-PIN or Bearer token header.
Parameterized SQL Enforced All database statements use ? positional parameter placeholders to prevent SQL injection.

System Architecture · Topology

System Topology & Component Architecture

Physical layout of the software across client browsers, edge ingress, server threads, Web Audio DSP pipelines, and local database storage.

1. End-to-End System Topology Diagram

The diagram below illustrates the exact pathways through which network requests, audio streams, and database writes flow. Use the controls to zoom, pan, or expand the diagram to full screen.

2. Detailed Subsystem Responsibilities

Tier 1: Client Applications & DSP

The frontend runs completely in the user's browser without external CDNs. It uses the Web Audio API to create a sound processing graph:

  • Buffer Decoding: Audio files are fetched and decoded into 32-bit floating point audio buffers in memory.
  • Telephone Simulation: When toggled on, audio routes through a Biquad bandpass filter (highpass at 300 Hz, lowpass at 3400 Hz) to simulate telephony call center acoustics.
  • Dynamic Waveform: HTML5 Canvas renders vertical peak bars, active playheads, and defect highlight overlays at 60 frames per second.

Tier 2: Ingress & Edge Network

Provides a secure bridge between mobile evaluators on the internet and the local host computer:

  • Automatic HTTPS: Terminating SSL/TLS at Cloudflare ensures mobile browsers allow Web Audio playback without security restrictions.
  • Outbound Connection: cloudflared establishes an outbound TCP/TLS session on port 7844. No incoming firewall ports or router NAT settings are opened.
  • Zero Billing Risk: Cloudflare Tunnel free tier has no data transfer quotas, eliminating overage charges.

Tier 3: Core Application Engine

run_server.py acts as the single backend process:

  • Multi-Threaded Server: Built on http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer. Each incoming request spawns a lightweight thread, allowing multiple evaluators to stream audio simultaneously.
  • HTTP Range Handler: Implements RFC 7233 byte-range parsing. Requests with Range: bytes=0-1024 return HTTP 206 with exact byte boundaries.
  • Admin Authorization: Verifies X-Admin-PIN header on all state mutations, while keeping public evaluation submission open for friction-free rating.

Tier 4: Storage & Persistence

All data is saved locally on the host computer's hard drive:

  • Relational Integrity: workbench.db operates with PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON; to prevent orphaned evaluation records or missing item references.
  • Safe Audio Directories: Uploaded audio files are validated and stored under public/uploads/ and audio/uploads/ with unique timestamps to prevent file overwrites.

System Architecture · Lifecycles

Request Lifecycles & Data Journeys

Chronological execution pathways, step timing budgets, and failure handling across client, tunnel, server threads, and the SQLite database.

Journey 1: Evaluator Scoring & Defect Submission Flow

Triggers when an evaluator selects Likert scores, highlights mispronounced words or waveform defect regions, types perceived speech differences, and clicks Submit & Next on eval.html.

Step Timing Budget Subsystem Concrete Operation & Failure Mode
Step 1 < 5 ms eval_app.js:1540 Gathers form inputs, Likert ratings, and defect regions into payload. Fails with UI warning if required scale is empty.
Step 2 15 - 40 ms Cloudflare Tunnel Encrypted transit over outbound TLS socket. Fails with HTTP 502 if local host computer is asleep.
Step 3 < 2 ms run_server.py:976 Extracts JSON body, checks payload validity, and generates unique evaluation ID (eval-[timestamp]-[hash]).
Step 4 4 - 8 ms database.py:124 Executes parameterized INSERT into evaluations table. Uses executemany for defect regions. Rolls back cleanly if foreign key is invalid.
Step 5 10 - 25 ms HTTP Response Sends HTTP 201 with {"success": true, "id": "..."}. Frontend automatically navigates to next audio item.

Journey 2: HTTP 206 Partial Content Audio Range Streaming

Triggers when a listener loads an audio sample, drags the playhead, or auditions an acoustic defect slice. Modern browsers require byte-range requests to support instant seeking without downloading the whole audio file first.

Phase HTTP Request / Response Physical Code Execution & Header Structure
1. Client Initial Probe GET /audio/model_a/KH01.wav
Range: bytes=0-		 Browser requests initial audio header to inspect sample rate (22050 Hz / 44100 Hz) and compute duration.
2. Server Range Parse run_server.py:175-220 Server reads physical file on disk (os.path.getsize), parses byte range, opens binary file, and seeks to byte offset.
3. Partial Content Delivery HTTP/1.1 206 Partial Content Sends headers:
Content-Range: bytes 0-1048575/2458920
Accept-Ranges: bytes
Content-Type: audio/wav
4. Timeline Scrubbing Range: bytes=1200000-2400000 When rater drags playhead to middle of waveform, browser requests only the targeted slice, preventing playback buffer stalls.

Journey 3: Study Creation, CSV Matching & Canvas Serialization

Triggers in admin.html when a researcher defines a study, uploads audio and paired transcripts, customizes UI components, and launches a campaign.

File Reconciliation Logic

Source: public/js/admin_app.js:1060

  • Filename Normalization: Strips folder paths and extensions (e.g., KH01.wav → kh01).
  • Safe Pairing: Matches CSV transcript rows against uploaded audio items by exact filename, stem, or prefix.
  • Pending CSV Buffer: If CSV is uploaded before audio files, rows are buffered in memory and matched automatically when audio files arrive.

Modular UI Config Serialization

Source: public/js/admin_app.js:2560

  • Canvas Block Array: Serializes playground components (Audio Player, Prompt Text, Word Tagger, Rubric, Transcription) into ui_config_json.
  • Dynamic Presentation: Stores font size (24px/32px/40px), blind-gating blur state, and default defect error codes.
  • Database Persistence: Saved directly to campaigns.ui_config_json in SQLite for 1:1 runtime rendering in eval.html.

Specifications · Relational Schema

Database Schema & Data Models

Full specification of SQLite tables in workbench.db, relational foreign key constraints, column data types, and indexing rules.

1. Database Invariants & Pragma Rules

The database layer is defined in database.py:30-165. Every connection opened by the server executes: 

PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;
PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL;

Foreign Key Cascades: Deleting a study (campaigns) or test suite automatically cascades to delete associated evaluations, defect tags, and rater scores without leaving orphaned records in the database.

2. Table: campaigns (Active Evaluation Studies)

Stores high-level evaluation studies, linking a prompt suite, scoring rubric, and UI component layout.

Column Name Type Key Default / Null Physical Responsibility & Relationships
id TEXT PK NOT NULL Unique campaign identifier (e.g. camp-dev23-4models).
project_id TEXT FK NOT NULL References projects(id) ON DELETE CASCADE.
name TEXT — NOT NULL Human-readable study title (e.g. Khmer Natural Voice Benchmark).
suite_id TEXT FK NOT NULL References test_suites(id) ON DELETE CASCADE.
rubric_id TEXT FK NOT NULL References rubrics(id) ON DELETE CASCADE.
ui_config_json TEXT — NULL JSON payload defining Step 3 canvas blocks, speeds, blind gating, and filters.
is_active INTEGER — 1 Binary status flag (1 = Active for raters, 0 = Paused/Closed).
created_at TIMESTAMP — CURRENT_TIMESTAMP UTC timestamp when study was created.

3. Table: evaluations (Rater Score Records)

Stores individual evaluator submissions for each test item and speech model candidate.

Column Name Type Key Default / Null Physical Responsibility & Relationships
id TEXT PK NOT NULL Unique evaluation identifier (e.g. eval-1795451589-9812).
campaign_id TEXT FK IDX NOT NULL References campaigns(id) ON DELETE CASCADE.
rater_id TEXT FK IDX NOT NULL References raters(id) ON DELETE CASCADE.
item_id TEXT FK IDX NOT NULL References test_items(id) ON DELETE CASCADE.
model_id TEXT FK IDX NOT NULL References models(id) ON DELETE CASCADE.
scores_json TEXT — NOT NULL JSON map of rubric dimensions to integer scores (e.g. {"naturalness":5}).
blind_transcript TEXT — NULL Text submitted by listener reporting perceived differences from prompt.
duration_seconds REAL — NULL Time in seconds the evaluator spent listening and rating this item.

4. Table: defect_tags (Acoustic Glitch Annotations)

Stores fine-grained timestamped defect regions and flagged word tokens.

Column Name Type Key Default / Null Physical Responsibility & Relationships
id TEXT PK NOT NULL Unique defect tag identifier.
evaluation_id TEXT FK IDX NOT NULL References evaluations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE.
error_code TEXT — NOT NULL Taxonomy code: MISPRON, NOISE, UNNAT_PAUSE, ROBOTIC, PITCH, OTHER.
word_text TEXT — NOT NULL Khmer word token or acoustic region label.
time_start_ms REAL — NULL Start timestamp in milliseconds on the waveform.
time_end_ms REAL — NULL End timestamp in milliseconds on the waveform.

5. Supporting Metadata Tables

Table Name Primary Key Core Stored Data Source Location
projects id (TEXT) Parent workspace and language metadata (e.g. Khmer language km). database.py:31

Operations · Deployment

$0 Free Hosting & Cloudflare Tunnel Guide

A comprehensive operational runbook for deploying Audio Studio publicly at zero cost without risk of database data loss or cloud overage fees.

1. Why Free Cloud PaaS Wipes Evaluation Data

Standard free cloud platforms (Render, Koyeb, Railway, and free-tier Hugging Face Spaces) are designed for stateless applications. Their free tiers run inside virtual containers with ephemeral filesystems:

Free Cloud PaaS Behavior

  • When no evaluator visits for 15 minutes, the server enters sleep mode to save compute.
  • When a new visitor arrives, the platform starts a fresh container from the original Git repository commit.
  • Fatal Result: Any changes written to workbench.db (all rater scores) and newly uploaded audio files in audio/uploads/ are permanently destroyed.

Cloudflare Host Tunnel Solution

  • The server runs on your local workstation, lab desktop, or campus PC.
  • workbench.db commits writes directly to your local solid-state drive (NVMe/SSD).
  • Result: Zero data loss. All evaluations are permanently saved on your drive, even if the tunnel restarts.

2. Step-by-Step Hosting Runbook

Operational Mode: Quick Public Tunnel (Instant Share)
Recommended

Use this mode to launch an immediate public evaluation link for testing cohorts without setting up domain records or Cloudflare accounts.

1

Open Terminal in repository root:

cd /Users/sorpheatepy/CADT/year-3/capstone/Audio-Studio
2

Launch the server with Mac sleep disabled:

caffeinate -d -i -m -s python3 run_server.py --port 8080 --share

caffeinate prevents macOS from entering sleep mode while your laptop lid remains open.

3

Distribute the link to evaluators:

The terminal will display a public HTTPS URL:

PUBLIC SHAREABLE LINK: https://[assigned-words].trycloudflare.com/eval

Send https://[assigned-words].trycloudflare.com/eval.html to your evaluators.

3. Permanent Free Custom Domains

Quick tunnels generate a new random URL if the server is stopped and restarted. To give your evaluators a permanent, fixed web address (such as audiostudio.yourdomain.com), follow these steps:

Step Platform Execution Details
1. Obtain Free Domain DuckDNS or is-a.dev Register a free subdomain (e.g. audiostudio.duckdns.org or audiostudio.is-a.dev). No credit card required.
2. Create Cloudflare Account dash.cloudflare.com Sign up for a free Cloudflare account with your email. Select the Free tier ($0).
3. Create Named Tunnel Zero Trust Dashboard Navigate to Networks → Tunnels → Create Tunnel. Name it audio-studio.
4. Route Hostname Public Hostname Settings Set domain to your subdomain and point the service to http://localhost:8080.

4. Continuous Integration (CI) Workflow

A GitHub Actions workflow is configured in .github/workflows/ci.yml. Whenever code is pushed to main or development, GitHub automatically runs two verification gates:

Gate 1: Automated Unit Tests

Command: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v

  • Runs 24 automated unit tests in an ephemeral in-memory database in ~1.4 seconds.
  • Tests database seed integrity, API endpoints, audio range requests, rater submissions, and admin authentication.

Gate 2: Package Integrity Validator

Command: python3 scripts/validate_package.py

  • Ensures all 23 core files exist and are UTF-8 readable.
  • Verifies that zero third-party dependencies have been introduced.
  • Validates all 20 benchmark test scenarios.

5. Database Snapshot & Backup Runbook

During live evaluation studies, perform regular database backups using SQLite's online backup API to prevent accidental data corruption: 

# Create a dated snapshot of workbench.db while server is running:
sqlite3 workbench.db ".backup backup_$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S).db"

# Export human-readable SQL dump:
sqlite3 workbench.db .dump > workbench_dump.sql
